article.title: How to Install Floor Transition Strips
article.summary: Pick the right transition molding for each doorway, leave room for a floating floor to move, and fasten the track so the strip sits flat and stays put.
article.body:
Transition strips cover the gap where two floors meet, in doorways or between rooms. This guide covers choosing the right profile and installing it so a floating floor can still expand and contract.

Affiliate disclosure: some links in this guide are affiliate links. If you buy through them, we may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. We only recommend products we'd use ourselves.

Safety: wear safety glasses when cutting, and check for pipes or radiant heat tubing in the floor before drilling into it.

Steps

  1. Choose the right profile

    A T-molding joins two floors of the same height. A reducer steps down from a thicker floor to a thinner one, such as vinyl plank to sheet vinyl. An end cap finishes an edge against a sliding door, fireplace or carpet. Many brands sell a 3-in-1 transition molding that can be set up as any of these.

    Done right: for each doorway you know which profile you need and how high each floor sits.

  2. Check the expansion gap

    A floating floor (vinyl plank or laminate) has to move. Leave the gap your flooring maker specifies between the two floors, often around 1/4 in on each side of where the track goes. The molding covers this gap and must never be screwed or glued down through the floating floor.

    Done right: there's an even gap along the whole doorway, wide enough for the track plus the expansion space.

  3. Measure and cut the track and molding

    Measure the doorway from jamb to jamb at floor level. Cut the track and the molding to that length with a fine-tooth saw. Test-fit both.

    Done right: the molding fits between the door jambs with no gap at either end.

  4. Fasten the track to the subfloor

    Center the track in the gap. On a wood subfloor, screw it down through the pre-drilled holes. On concrete, use construction adhesive or the anchors the kit specifies.

    Done right: the track is centered, straight and doesn't move when you push on it.

  5. Press the molding into place

    Line the molding up over the track and press it down. Lay a scrap of wood on top and tap it with a rubber mallet along its length until it snaps in fully. For a reducer, make sure the low edge rests on the lower floor.

    Done right: the strip sits flat with no rocking, and the door swings over it without catching.

Get help if: the floors differ in height by more than your reducer can cover, or the subfloor in the doorway is uneven or soft. A custom-cut threshold or subfloor repair may be needed first.

FAQ

Do I need a transition strip between rooms?

For floating floors, usually yes at doorways and long runs, because the floor needs expansion gaps. Check your flooring's instructions for the maximum run without a break.

Can I glue a transition strip to vinyl plank flooring?

Not to a floating floor. Fasten the track or adhesive to the subfloor in the gap so the floor can still move under the strip.

What transition goes between vinyl plank and carpet?

Use an end cap or a carpet-to-hard-surface transition so the carpet edge tucks under or meets it neatly.
